verdict.rationale: Vercel plugs into existing GitHub, GitLab, and Bitbucket workflows and deploys on every push. It supports 40+ frameworks, offers an Apache-2.0 CLI that runs from automated systems, and publishes a file-system Build Output API spec plus Dockerfile-based container deploys that reduce lock-in. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of integration with third-party CI systems (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI) beyond the CLI's automated-system mention, editor-workflow evidence beyond AI coding-tool plugins, and independent hands-on corroboration of a lock-in-free workflow.

support.subject: As a developer, I can keep using my existing Git, CI, editor, and framework workflows without adopting proprietary tooling

citations.quote: Connect GitHub, GitLab, or Bitbucket to deploy on every push, with a preview URL for every branch.
Deploy Next.js with zero configuration, or bring one of 40+ supported frameworks.
With the command-line interface (CLI) you can interact with the Vercel platform using a terminal, or through an automated system
The Build Output API is a file-system-based specification for a directory structure that can produce a Vercel deployment.
Run any code and library on Vercel Functions with an OCI container image built from a Dockerfile or Containerfile at the project root.
Works with Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Grok Build, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, and Kimi Code.
